notes: Loop 3 (loop 2: 5.0, capped; about 8.4 without the cap). I rebuilt these by hand: the lunch demo (5.35/6.54/1.19, 13.57, 23.00, break-even 54.57 ÷ 5.35 → 11, keep from 7, −385.20/−117.70/+256.80, worst −545.70, €862, tornado 642/223.5/209.5/180.9); /try with 11,20 € (−1/+266/+641, worst −162, break-even 4) and without a lunch spend (worst +100, shown as 'Selbst im schlimmsten Fall kein Verlust'); the price demo (2.33/2.50, −6.8%, 43.40 − 42.00 = +1.40); both result demos (−184.20 tweak, +125.80 keep). All right, German included. The cap is lifted: every milk-drink text in all four languages gives 7% only to take away (messages.ts:150/171/210-212/511, de :132/152/190-192/494, report-price.txt:138-147). I opened every fact link: §12 Abs. 2 Nr. 15 ('mit Ausnahme der Abgabe von Getränken'), Anlage 2 Nr. 35 (75% milk), MiLoV5 (€13.90/€14.60, 5 Nov 2025) and the BMF PDF of 22 Dec 2025 (30% for Kombiangebote). Edge cases give plain words; 123 engine tests pass. Held back: the price demo answers that the 20 cents cover the 2027 rise, but only before employer contributions (about 21%; about 31% on a Minijob). With them, +€1.40 becomes about −€7 to −€12 a week. Also uneven rounding (−536 € vs 537 €) and module state.
improvements: The wage-rise verdict leaves out employer contributions, and the shipped price demo sits right on that edge. src/engine/price-change.ts:134-156 (priceWageRise: costWeek = hours × €0.70, covers = leftWeek ≥ 0), messages.ts:450-452 (price.wage.plain.covers/short/none) and the same keys in de/es/pl, src/report/sections.ts:489-500 (the card) and src/report/demo.ts:41-49 (60 h, +20 cents). /r#demo-price says 'Der neue Preis trägt die Lohnerhöhung also, und es bleiben etwa 1,40 € pro Woche übrig, vor Arbeitgeberanteilen' (report-price.txt:216). Employers pay about 21% on top for an employee and 31.17% flat for a commercial Minijob in 2026, so the €42 rise really costs €51-55. Then the 20 cents fall €7-12 a week short. The engine knows this cost: staff_hourly_cost asks for 'wage plus employer contributions', and lunch.warn.belowMinWage says they 'come on top'. Fix: add an optional employer_share field (fallback 21%, tagged a guess, with a note 'Minijob: about 31%; your payroll shows it'). Compute costWeek = hours × €0.70 × (1 + share), with the maths 'wage €42.00 + contributions €8.82 = €50.82', and base covers on it. Also, 'at or near the minimum wage' charges €0.70 for every hour; ask instead for hours paid below €14.60. Criterion: correctness and honesty (the demo's one question gets the wrong answer for most owners). Done when /r#demo-price no longer says 'covers' for +€1.40 against €42, and a test pins the sum with contributions in all four languages.

Uneven rounding shows one number two ways. format.ts:56-61 (money) and src/report/html.ts:130-134 (wholeSigned) use Math.round, which rounds −x.5 towards zero. Plain sentences instead round the absolute value (eur(Math.abs(x)), format.ts:132). Example: the German lunch demo with vat_rate moved from 10.6% to 19% gives worst_case −536.50. whatChanged's effects say '−536 €', and the sentence next to them says 'kostet der Test jetzt 537 € statt 546 €'. On /r#demo-price the wage card's bar shows 'Bleibt pro Woche +1 €', while the text under it says 'etwa 1,40 €' (report-price.txt:213-216). Fix: have money() and wholeSigned() use the sign-symmetric round() from format.ts:73 (half away from zero), and draw amounts under €10 with cents in the bars, as eur() does. Criterion: correctness (rounding never changes a figure between two places). Done when a test with −536.5 finds the same digits in effects and plain, and the wage bar reads +1,40 €.

The gain case has sign words that read as losses. messages.ts:232 (lunch.label.fromSwitching 'gained from regulars who switch') and :237 (lunch.be.maths.free) produce '−10,03 € Gewinn durch wechselnde Stammgäste = −10,03 € pro Tag: Es bleibt nichts zu decken'. The keep-number maths says 'Wechselnde Stammgäste und laufende Kosten ergeben −10,03 € pro Tag'. An owner reaches this from /try by leaving the lunch spend empty, which derives it from 7,40 €. Write 'Wechselnde Stammgäste bringen 10,03 € pro Tag mehr, die laufenden Kosten sind 0,00 €: es bleibt nichts zu decken.' Likewise, price.wage.plain.none (messages.ts:452) says a cut 'brings no extra money (−€38 a week), so it does nothing towards the minimum-wage rise'. It costs €38 on top of the €42, so say 'it costs you €38 a week more, so with the €42 wage rise you are €80 a week short'. Criterion: transparency (plain German, no sign the reader must flip). Done when no maths line puts a minus in front of 'Gewinn', 'gained' or their es/pl words, checked by a test over the gain case in four languages.

Carried over: one source of truth for language and currency, and no money arithmetic in the report. format.ts:14 still has 'let currency'. experiment.ts:21-22 and compare.ts:61-63 and :198-199 still call setLang/setCurrency as side effects. src/report/sections.ts:600-610 keeps the slider fallbacks (p.netTest − gp.netTest, perTest ÷ days, dx × per × days). The new sections.ts:467-470 adds one more (gainWeek = left + cost), although src/engine/index.ts already offers wageRiseCheck for older analyses. Pass lang and currency as arguments. Have the report call wageRiseCheck, and delete the report-side fallbacks. Criterion: code a reviewer can follow, no money outside src/engine. Done when grep finds no setCurrency outside index.ts entry points and no arithmetic on netTest or leftWeek in src/report.

Fact polish and one demo per template. (a) fact.vat_food_7 says '7% since 1 January 2026 (eat-in and take-away)' with the source § 12 Abs. 2 Nr. 15 UStG. Take-away food was already 7% (Nr. 1 with Anlage 2); only eat-in changed in 2026, as the milk fact already says of its own rule. Split it: 'eat-in: 7% since 1 Jan 2026 (Nr. 15); take-away: 7% already before (Anlage 2)'. (b) Add the gazette entry to the source: Steueränderungsgesetz 2025, BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 363 of 23 Dec 2025. (c) min_wage_2027 shows 'Stand: 1. Januar 2027', an as-of date in the future. Use the MiLoV5 date (5 Nov 2025) as Stand, and keep 'ab 1. Januar 2027' in the value. (d) demoInputs('price_change') is +30 cents (templates.ts:47, the MCP demo: +€91.02 against €42), but src/report/demo.ts:579-581 sets new_price to +20 cents outside the engine. Keep one price demo, defined in src/engine. Criterion: transparency of sources. Done when the facts card dates each rule by when it took effect and the MCP and site demos give the same wage answer.
